rationale:
Decision: resubmit the iteration 10 design unchanged, because it is the best raced result (58.8527) and the only confirmed design on the development tracks. Both the round-1 critique and the round-2 critique argued against an untested change on the final iteration, and I agree. The draft's kp 3.0 / kd 1.5 / sensor_size 0.012 / wheel_track 0.14 / mass 0.6 design was a misread baseline and is withdrawn.

What the evidence shows: all 60 trials ended off_track with 0 completions. Progress is 0.11 to 0.17. Scores come from partial progress and the line-loss and rms terms. Iterations 7 and 8 differ only in base_speed (1.5 vs 1.3) and give identical results, so base_speed is not the limiting factor. Iteration 9 (sensor_size 0.008) and iteration 6 (sensor_size 0.012, y 0.06) both score below iteration 10, so 0.016 at y 0.08 is the best measured sensor setting.

Corrections to the round-2 critique, which I checked against the outcome table: (1) I withdraw my earlier claim that kd has no measurable effect. Iterations 7 and 8 do not vary kd, so the kd effect is untested here, not shown to be absent. (2) I withdraw the stall explanation. The telemetry shows every run ends off_track, not stalled, so track length and stall do not explain the low progress. (3) The steady-offset explanation for ki 0 is a hypothesis without per-step telemetry, so I do not rely on it.

What I kept: the y = 0.08 sensor row with x from -0.03 to 0.03, weights -1 to 1, sensor_size 0.016, kp 4.5, kd 0.1, ki 0, base_speed 1.5, line_loss last_direction, wheel_track 0.12, wheel_radius 0.03, mass 0.8, body 0.18 by 0.12. Changing any of these is untested at this combination, and the critique's suggested kp 3.5 change is rejected for the same reason.

Risks accepted: the held-back track is a different shape, and the design leaves the line on every development track, so an off_track result on the final track is likely. The expected score on the unseen track is uncertain, and I expect roughly 58.85 only if the held-back bends resemble the development tracks.
